recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No current core source follow-up is recommended for FHIR-5546 unless Patient Care reopens the broader Condition/Concern modeling question in a new tracker.
issue_request: FHIR-5546 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification DSTU1 Patient Care request to clarify whether Condition represents a point-in-time event or a longer-lived concern/problem-list item, with a proposed separate Concern resource if needed. The recorded motions called for analysis of Condition vs. concern and clarification that Condition could be used as a point-in-time observation of a condition event.
initial_application: No source commit explicitly naming FHIR-5546 was found. The Jira comments say Condition scope/introduction changes were applied based on GF#10090, and git history shows df58ee3f55 applying '#10090 Condition Introduction updates' to source/condition/condition-introduction.xml. That commit introduced the broad wording that Condition can be a point-in-time diagnosis, a practitioner Problem List item, or a concern outside the Problem List.
additional_context: FHIR-10090 is a Published/Persuasive same-artifact decision to broaden the Condition introduction beyond clinician-only and medical-state-only wording, including patient concerns and lack of stakeholder consensus. FHIR-10614 was closed as a duplicate pointing to FHIR-10090 for reviewing/expanding Condition scope. Later Published issues FHIR-26904 and FHIR-38954 refined Observation boundaries and example wording while preserving the concern/problem-list model. Direct Zulip and Confluence issue-key searches found no conflicting community record.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. The current Condition source is in build scope and already says Condition can be a point-in-time diagnosis, an item on a practitioner's Problem List, or a concern that is not on that Problem List; it also clarifies when symptoms should be Observations. A source edit to make Condition point-in-time-only would conflict with the applied and later published decisions.
